notes: This file is the single source of truth for all emission factors used by carbon_calculator.py. The calculation engine must never hardcode a numeric factor outside this file. Every factor below is either (a) an India-specific sourced value, (b) a disclosed international proxy, or (c) an explicitly labeled assumption. Category 'shopping' is intentionally excluded from numeric calculation -- see qualitative_only flag.

walking.notes: No direct combustion emissions; consistent with standard calculator convention.

bus.source: India GHG Program (WRI India / TERI / CII) - India Specific Road Transport Emission Factors
bus.geographic_scope: India (intracity buses, State Transport Utility fleet average)
bus.calculation_method: Weighted average across State Road Transport Utilities: diesel consumption (from revenue-km / fuel efficiency) x fuel emission factor, divided by total passenger-km
bus.assumptions: Assumes standard intracity occupancy patterns from CIRT/SRTU data.
bus.limitations: NOT valid for Bus Rapid Transit (BRTS) or intercity buses -- loading and passenger-km differ significantly for those services.

two_wheeler_standard.source: India GHG Program - India Specific Road Transport Emission Factors
two_wheeler_standard.represents: Scooter <150cc (e.g. Activa-class) -- includes study's 10% uplift factor
two_wheeler_standard.calculation_method: Fuel emission factor (2.27193 kg CO2/litre petrol) / average fleet fuel efficiency, +10% uplift for real-world conditions
two_wheeler_standard.assumptions: Used as representative of the most common two-wheeler segment in India.
two_wheeler_standard.limitations: Actual value ranges 0.0319-0.0597 kg/km across the full engine-capacity range the source studied (100cc-500cc); this is a simplification for a short user questionnaire, not the full granularity available.

two_wheeler_premium.source: India GHG Program - India Specific Road Transport Emission Factors

car_shared_metadata.source: India GHG Program (WRI India / TERI / CII) - India Specific Road Transport Emission Factors
car_shared_metadata.calculation_method: Fuel emission factor (petrol 2.27193 kg CO2/L, diesel 2.6444 kg CO2/L) divided by SIAM-segment average fuel efficiency, +8% uplift factor (per CRRI real-world driving study) applied by the source
car_shared_metadata.confidence: high -- verified directly against primary source PDF, section 5.3.1
car_shared_metadata.assumptions: Each simplified UI category (Small/Hatchback/Sedan/SUV x Petrol/Diesel/Hybrid) maps to one representative sub-segment from the source's ~24 car categories, chosen to match common Indian market models.
car_shared_metadata.limitations: Real emissions vary further by exact engine size and vehicle age/condition within each bucket; this is a defensible simplification, not full precision.

grid_average.source: Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Government of India - CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, Version 21.0
grid_average.calculation_method: Total CO2 emissions from grid-connected stations / net electricity generation into grid (includes thermal, hydro, nuclear, RES, and imports)
grid_average.assumptions: Uses national average; does not adjust for state-level grid mix (e.g. West Bengal's coal-heavy mix vs. a hydro-heavy state).
grid_average.limitations: Marked provisional by CEA. Declines annually as renewable share grows (0.727 in FY23-24, 0.716 in FY22-23) -- should be reviewed/updated yearly.

diet.source: Scarborough, P. et al. (2014), 'Dietary greenhouse gas emissions of meat-eaters, fish-eaters, vegetarians and vegans in the UK', Climatic Change
diet.geographic_scope: United Kingdom (EPIC-Oxford cohort, ~55,000 participants) -- used as an international proxy; no equivalent India-specific large-cohort study was found
diet.assumptions: User's self-selected diet category is mapped directly to the closest matching UK cohort category.
diet.limitations: Indian dietary patterns (dairy-heavy vegetarian diets, different staples, different food-mile patterns) differ materially from the UK cohort this data was drawn from. This MUST be disclosed to the end user as a proxy, not an Indian-specific figure.

base_factor.source: 'The Greenhouse Gas Emission of Mumbai City' (2026), Springer Nature -- India-specific municipal waste management case study
base_factor.geographic_scope: Mumbai, India -- used as a national proxy
base_factor.calculation_method: Total emissions from the city's current waste management mix (landfill + partial treatment) / total MSW tonnage; rounded from measured 0.998 kg CO2e/kg
base_factor.assumptions: Used as a directional national estimate.
base_factor.limitations: City-specific figure; India's MSW collection/treatment rate varies significantly by city and state (national collection rate ~70-75% per CPCB-adjacent sources).

recycling_reduction.rationale: Reasonable simplification representing that consistent recycling diverts a meaningful share of waste from landfill/high-emission disposal.
recycling_reduction.confidence: low -- explicitly disclosed as an assumption, not derived from a study
recycling_reduction.limitations: No authoritative India-specific household-level recycling-avoided-emissions figure was found. Must be labeled as an assumption in both code comments and any user-facing methodology page.

shopping.rationale: No India-specific, methodologically defensible per-item or per-spend emission factor was found. Including a fabricated number here would manufacture false precision. This category is passed to the AI (Granite) as context for generating advice, and shown to the user as a separate qualitative indicator -- never added into the CO2e total.

reference_points_for_context_only.note: These are NOT used in calculation. Provided only as background for writing sensible AI prompt context.
reference_points_for_context_only.source: GoClimate, 'The carbon footprint of shopping' (2020) -- non-peer-reviewed, illustrative only
reference_points_for_context_only.examples: t-shirt ~2 kg CO2e, jeans ~15-20 kg CO2e (embedded manufacturing footprint, global average)

display.disclosure_note: Indicative estimate based on published emission factors, documented proxies, and stated assumptions. It is not a complete life-cycle assessment.
